name: Lanser See
kurzbeschreibung: Lake Lanser See at 836 m on the Innsbruck plateau is a heritage peat-water bathing tarn featuring healing moor mud, a vintage lido, walking loops, and Nordkette views.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The enchanting Lake Lanser See rests at an elevation of 836 metres on the sun-blessed southeastern plateau above Tirol's regional capital Innsbruck, situated within the municipality of Lans. Covering approximately 3.5 hectares with depths reaching twelve metres, this idyllic woodland tarn ranks among the oldest and most cherished summer swimming waters for Innsbruck residents. Formed in a post-glacial depression, the lake is fed by pure subterranean springs and mineral-rich peat runoff. In midsummer, the dark, velvety moor water warms swiftly to 23 to 25 degrees Celsius, celebrated for its soothing dermatological benefits. Framed by fragrant reed beds and mixed forest, the sprawling sunbathing lawns present arresting vistas of the jagged limestone Nordkette ridge to the north and Mount Patscherkofel to the south. A heritage-listed timber lido equipped with diving platforms, paddle boats, and lakeside dining preserves nostalgic summer holiday flair.

Route & Anforderungen

Circling Lake Lanser See is an easy, two-kilometre stroll taking roughly 30 to 45 minutes of relaxed walking with negligible elevation gain. The level gravel path meanders beneath shaded trees, passing lily-dappled wetlands where waterfowl and dragonflies thrive. For an expanded excursion, walkers can link the lake with the adjacent Lanser Moor water-lily pond or follow forest trails descending to historic Ambras Castle above Innsbruck (approx. 1.5 to 2 hours). Pathways are broad, barrier-free, and ideally suited for prams and wheelchairs. Comfortable walking sneakers are entirely sufficient.

Besuch & Anreise

Motorists ascend from Innsbruck via the southeastern mountain road to Lans, where designated paid parking is available. A remarkably scenic and romantic transit option is boarding the heritage Tram Line 6 (Mittelgebirgsbahn), which winds through tranquil pine forests from Bergisel straight to Lanser See station.

Tipps

Conclude your visit on the water's edge terrace of the 'Koi Bar am Lanser See'. Savoring artisanal pastries while watching the evening sun cast golden reflections across the water toward the Nordkette peaks is pure alpine bliss.
preis: Walking trails freely accessible; Lanser See beach lido charges admission during summer months
oeffnungszeiten: Lakeside trails open year-round; bathing establishment operates May through September
